Pages read on rendered images at 90-110 dpi by the PC-S55-A research: PDF p. 41 (printed p. 17, April, XXXVIII Item alia, the prayer Tribue nos Dne quaesumus donis tuis libera mente servire, with note 2, Mur. and Ball. emendemur); PDF pp. 147, 149 and 150 (printed pp. 123, 125 and 126: September, XXVIIII In natale episcoporum, its Mass III Item alia from p. 125, and on p. 126 the prayer Gaudeat Dne quaesumus populus ... caelestium rerum frequentatione proficiat ut et temporalibus beneficiis adiuvetur et erudiatur aeternis). Page rule measured on these pages: PDF page = printed page + 24 in the body of the edition.
artifacts.rights_basis: C. L. Feltoe's Sacramentarium Leonianum (Cambridge: at the University Press, 1896) is in the United States public domain by date of publication (first published abroad before 1931, as derived for calendar year 2026 under guidance/missals.md). This exact file is the Internet Archive's 2011 digitization of the University of Toronto (PIMS) copy; a mechanical digitization of a public-domain printing adds no original authorship, and the file carries no digitiser notice page. The entire 19,868,448-byte file is retained as a reasonably sized reusable facsimile, as the 28,655,931-byte Wilson 1915 Gregorian scan is.

work.author: Catholic Church
work.description: The earliest surviving collection of Roman Mass formularies, a libellus collection copied at Verona in the earlier seventh century and preserving material of the fifth and sixth. It is not an ordered sacramentary and has no Advent or Lent; its formularies run by month from April. Long called Leonine on an attribution to Leo the Great that is not now maintained, and catalogued under both names.
work.title: Sacramentarium Veronense
